title: Set texts (tags only)
examples: Do I have to read every book on the list?
How does the set text influence my essay?
What if I don't like the required novel?

explain.say: Today we will look at set texts in literature.

draw.text: Set Text Lists: What are they?

explain.say: A set text means a group of books studied together.
These texts often explore a shared big idea or theme.
The curriculum will tell you which texts are set for your year.
For example, if you study a set text on war, you might read a novel and a poem.
In real life, a set text might be a collection of poems about a specific time period.

faq.q: Do I have to read every single book listed as a set text?
faq.a: Yes, generally you are expected to read all the texts listed for your course. These texts form the core of your study. You might also hear people ask if reading all texts is mandatory, or what happens if I skip a text.
asks: What if I don't finish the reading?

faq.q: How does knowing the set texts help me write my essays?
faq.a: Knowing the set texts gives you a common pool of ideas and themes to draw from. You can compare how different authors handle the same topic. Others might ask how to link texts in an essay, or what themes are common to the set texts.
asks: How do I compare texts in my essay?
What is the purpose of the set texts?

faq.q: If the set texts are from different countries, do I need to know the background?
faq.a: It is very helpful to know the historical or cultural background of the texts. This context helps you understand the author's message better. You could ask about the historical context, or what the setting means.
asks: How does history affect the literature?

faq.q: What is the difference between a set text and recommended reading?
faq.a: Set texts are specifically chosen for your curriculum study. Recommended reading is extra material you can read for enjoyment or deeper study. You might ask what the difference is, or if I should read the recommended books.
asks: Should I focus on set or recommended texts?

faq.q: Can I focus my essay on just one set text?
faq.a: While you can focus on one text, the best essays often compare ideas across multiple set texts. Comparing shows a deeper understanding of the theme. You might ask if single-text essays are acceptable, or how to compare texts effectively.
asks: How many texts should I compare?

facts: Set texts are pieces of literature chosen for a specific course.
They allow students to compare how different authors treat similar themes.
The curriculum guide will specify which texts are set for a particular year group.

quiz.say: When comparing texts, what is the main benefit?
quiz.why: Comparing texts shows you how the theme can be viewed from different angles.

wrong.0: Length is not the goal; depth of thought is.
wrong.1: Comparison does not guarantee avoiding criticism.
wrong.2: This defeats the purpose of studying a 'set' group.

quiz.say: A teacher tells you that this year's set texts are 'The Crucible' and 'Animal Farm'. What are you likely studying?
quiz.why: Both texts are famous examples used to critique power structures.

wrong.0: These texts are more focused on societal issues than family life.
wrong.1: They deal with serious political themes, not just romance.
wrong.2: While they have journeys, the focus is on real-world politics.
